# BF-188: recount PM-089's unclaimed library functions against today's open PRs and main, with title hits flagged
from: Bug Finder
for: any
priority: high

## Why
The user, 2026-10-24 (relayed by the PM): "we want to be on top of these along side any bug fixes/bug fix requests". PM-089's claim data is from 2026-10-22 01:00 UTC. Since then many of its rows' blockers merged, and others' PRs took rows. Coverage batches are being posted from it (BF-189 to BF-193); this recount is what the next batches come from.

## What
1. **Inputs on `cloud-results`:**
   - PM-088: `results/cloud-3/PM-088.md` and `results/cloud-3/PM-088/<library>.tsv`, the per-function class (A, B-S, B-M, B-L, C, D) and basis;
   - PM-089: `results/cloud-2/PM-089.md`, `results/cloud-2/PM-089/batches.tsv` and its per-row claim file, and the method in its "Method" section. Reuse that method.
2. **Base:** `git fetch upstream main` (use `upstream`, never `origin`). Today's open upstream PRs are in the first data block below: number, head SHA and author, as of 2026-10-24T23:47Z (1,291 PRs). This session has GitHub API access; yours doesn't, so take this list as the open set. Fetch heads with `git fetch upstream refs/pull/<n>/head`, and check the fetched SHA matches.
3. **For each of PM-088's implementable rows** (classes A, B-S, B-M and C-real, the 1,031 PM-089 counted), give one status:
   - **done on main:** main's body no longer throws `NotImplemented_nid_no_patch` (or the function is now implemented there);
   - **claimed by #N:** an open PR changes that function's body, by PM-089's rules. List every claiming PR, with its author;
   - **unclaimed.**
4. **Flag title hits.** The second data block lists every function name a title report shows hitting "not implemented", from upstream issues and our sweeps, with the issues and title IDs. Flag each row whose function is in it.
5. **Re-batch the unclaimed rows the way PM-089 did:**
   - one library per batch, 10-30 functions, small enough for one reviewable PR;
   - title-hit rows first, then A and B-S, then B-M and C-real;
   - each batch names what it waits on: an open PR that adds a helper, file or state it builds on, or a sibling PR to stay out of the way of;
   - mark which of BF-189 to BF-193's rows (posted with this task) are now claimed or done, so those batches can drop them.
6. **Badge estimate:** redo PM-089's section 4 with today's numbers.

## Result
- `results/cloud-<n>/BF-188.md`, text only:
  - counts per library: done on main, claimed and unclaimed;
  - the title-hit rows still unclaimed;
  - the new batches, ranked;
  - the badge estimate.
- `results/cloud-<n>/BF-188/rows.tsv`, with the columns `library, function, class, status, claimed_by, title_hits, batch`.
- Read-only work: no code changes and no branches.

## When you finish

After you mark this task done, claim the next open task on the board right away (priority high first, then the lowest id; skip any whose `for:` line names another worker). If none is open, restart the board watcher as a background command before you end your turn. A worker that ends its turn with no task and no watcher is never woken: on 2026-10-15 one sat READY for 30 minutes beside two open tasks.
